## Intent
Hypothesis: identity-ordered per-particle blend with no intermediates can approach the streaming ceiling at low death rates, with scatter cost isolated from cache effects.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill (N≈963) is below the measured range. At N=10000 (680 KB working set, in L2), ns/p is 6.5–8.6 at q=0.01; cost FALLS to 5.4–6.1 at N=100000 as overhead amortizes. The L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 produces no knee — ns/p stays FLAT at ~5.4–5.9 from N=100000 through N=10000000. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the N-curve: at q=0.5 the worst trials sit at ~11.1 ns/p across all N while best trials reach 5.9–6.4, widening variance rather than shifting shape.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 12.59 GB/s at N=100000, q=0.01 — 42% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.01 the algo sustains 11.6–12.6 GB/s across N=100000–10000000 with no falloff. The profile shows 70–80% compute and 13–19% backend stall at q=0.01, so it is compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound, in the low-churn regime. Branch_flush climbs from 4.7% (q=0.01) to 45.1% (q=0.5, threads=1); worst-trial bandwidth drops to 6.08 GB/s (20% of ceiling). The transition to branch-bound occurs by q=0.25, where branch_flush hits 32.3%.

## Assembly
No vectorization — vector-suffixed instructions: 0. All floating-point is scalar: `ldp s5, s6`, `ldp s7, s16`, `ldr s17` load one particle's fields; `fadd s5`, `fmul s5`, `fcvtzs` process them individually. The grid scatter is byte-granular read-modify-write: `ldrb w2, [x1]`, `add w2, w2, w12`, `cmp w2, #0xff`, `csel w2, w2, w11, lo`, `strb w2, [x1]` — 16 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` total. This scalar byte-scatter caps bandwidth at 42% of ceiling and drives the 70–80% compute fraction. The 20 `csel` and 24 `cmp` implement per-particle saturation and bounds checks; 20 `b` plus 4 `cbz` and 4 `tbnz` create the branchy control flow whose flushes dominate at high death rates.

## Verdict
Partially — the N-curve is flat past the L2 spill (5.4–5.9 ns/p at q=0.01 from N=100000 onward), confirming cache behavior is not the limiter. But the algo never exceeds 12.59 GB/s (42% of ceiling) because zero vectorization and the byte-granular `strb`/`ldrb` scatter prevent streaming, and by q=0.5 branch_flush reaches 45.1% with worst-trial bandwidth collapsing to 6.08 GB/s. The hypothesis holds only for cache-insensitivity; the streaming-ceiling claim is refuted.
